title: Signed insertion identities for the complement of a chain retraction
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $r\in\mathbb N$, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$, $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $i:\operatorname{Fin}(r)$. Let $A$ and $C$ be the restriction to $U_i$ of the integer extensions of $G[0]$ and the explicit alternating complex [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction], with restricted augmentation $a:A\to C$. For every chain morphism $q:C\to A$ such that $a\circ q=1_A$ (Lean composition order), there are module morphisms $h_k:C^{k+1}\to C^k$ for all $k\in\mathbb Z$ satisfying $(q\circ a)^k+d_k h_k+h_{k-1}d_{k-1}=1_{C^k}$. The second composite uses the canonical identification $C^k\cong C^{k-1+1}$; all compositions are written in Lean order.

source.place: Tag 02FU, local insertion and degree-zero projection; ordered adaptation using Tag 01FM; parent insertion-homotopy proof

proof.text: Obtain the singleton degree-zero map and the nonnegative insertion operators from the singleton-contraction statement. The restricted extended source is zero away from degree zero, since it is the extension of a single complex; the restricted target is zero in negative degrees. These support properties follow directly from isZero_single_obj_X, isZero_extend_X, extendXIso and restriction map_isZero.

Extend the degree-zero map to a chain map p:C→A by zero elsewhere. The chain equation with target degree zero has source degree minus one, which is zero; every other target degree is zero. The insertion identity holds in negative degrees by IsZero, in degree zero by the singleton equation with the incoming differential zero, and in positive degrees by the stated insertion equation and p.f k=0. Build the homotopy H:id_C~p≫a by transporting h_k to the component from j to k whenever k+1=j and using zero off this relation. The insertion identities verify Homotopy.comm by additive rearrangement.

For the supplied q, associativity and a≫q=id imply (p≫a)≫(q≫a)=p≫a. Postcompose H with q≫a, then compose with the equality homotopy. This gives a homotopy id_C≫(q≫a)~p≫a. Reverse it and compose with H to obtain K:id_C~q≫a. Set the requested h_k=K.hom(k+1,k). Rewrite Homotopy.comm using dNext_eq and prevD_eq; transport its incoming term with XIsoOfEq and reorder the three additive terms. This proves the required equation at every integer k, with no further sorry.

lean.statement:
theorem alternatingCechSheafAugmentation_restrict_insertion_identities
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {r : ℕ} (U : Fin r → X.Opens) (G : X.Modules) (i : Fin r) :
    let F := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι
    let A := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      (((CochainComplex.single₀ X.Modules).obj G).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    let C := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      ((alternatingCechSheafComplex U G).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    let a := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map
      (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (alternatingCechSheafAugmentation U G)
        ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    ∀ q : C ⟶ A, a ≫ q = 𝟙 A →
      ∃ h : ∀ k : ℤ, C.X (k + 1) ⟶ C.X k,
        ∀ k : ℤ, (q ≫ a).f k + C.d k (k + 1) ≫ h k +
          (C.XIsoOfEq (show k = k - 1 + 1 by omega)).hom ≫
            h (k - 1) ≫ C.d (k - 1) k = 𝟙 (C.X k)
